description:
Somos entusiastas de la ingeniería de sistemas, el desarrollo de software y la exploración espacial. Creemos firmemente que la tecnología y la programación son las herramientas clave para rescatar y visibilizar la historia de las misiones pasadas.
Buscamos mentes creativas y entusiastas con talento para colaborar mano a mano.
summary:
We developed an interactive web application designed as a historical space telemetry archive to bring to life NASA’s exploration vehicles remaining on the Moon (LRV-1, LRV-2, and LRV-3 from Apollo 15, 16, and 17) and Mars (Spirit and Opportunity).

To address the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge, we transformed NASA’s scientific data and historical records into an immersive audiovisual experience. Rather than relying on text-heavy pages, users with a special focus on children and young learners can explore interactive landing maps, rotate and zoom 3D rover models, and listen to narrated stories powered by voice synthesis. This project matters because it makes science communication accessible, sparks early curiosity in STEM fields, and preserves the human and technological legacy of space exploration for future generations.
details:
What it does and how it works

The platform simulates an Earth Observatory terminal that allows users to navigate between two planetary destinations: the Moon and Mars. Upon selecting a celestial body, users can view environmental data (gravity and temperature), exact landing coordinates on interactive maps, and mission telemetry cards (distance traveled, mission duration, key findings, and last contact date). It also features an integrated audio player with a real-time waveform visualizer to listen to each vehicle's story, alongside interactive 3D viewers to rotate and zoom into the Martian rovers from any angle.

Benefits and Expected Impact

- Inclusive and Accessible Learning: By prioritizing audio storytelling over dense reading, the platform makes space history accessible to young children, users with reading difficulties or visual impairments, and the general public.

- Inspiring Future STEM Explorers: It transforms raw technical metrics into relatable, engaging stories that spark curiosity in space exploration, engineering, and astronomy.

Tools, Programming Languages, and Software Used

- Web Development & Data Architecture: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (ES6+) for interactive logic and DOM manipulation, paired with JSON files to cleanly structure mission metadata, coordinates, and telemetry metrics.

- 3D Visualization: Integration of interactive 3D models based on official NASA assets for the Spirit and Opportunity rovers.

- Artificial Intelligence & Audio Synthesis: Google Gemini was used to synthesize, adapt, and translate official NASA documentation into an engaging, child-friendly narrative script; ElevenLabs (Text-to-Speech) was used to generate natural, expressive voiceovers.

- Development Environment: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) and GitHub for version control and project hosting.

Creativity and Key Factors Considered by the Team

Our project's creativity lies in blending the visual atmosphere of a deep-space telemetry console with warm, accessible storytelling tailored for children. Our team prioritized two core factors: attention retention (replacing long text blocks with voice narration and manipulable 3D models) and scientific accuracy (grounding every coordinate, metric, and story directly in NASA’s historical records).
